descriptionChirho: Masculine noun denoting a friend, companion, or close associate. Used of personal relationships: Ahuzzath, Abimelech's 'friend' (Gen 26:26 mērēʿēhū 'his friend'), Samson's companions at his wedding feast (Judg 14:11,20 mērēʿīm 'companions'; 15:2,6 'his/your companion'), the friends of David who sent him gifts from the spoil (2 Sam 3:8 mērēʿēhū 'his friends'), and the proverbial observation that a poor man's friends abandon him (Prov 19:7 mērēʿēhū 'his friends'). Multilingual glosses are consistent: arb ṣāḥib/aṣdiqāʾ (companion/friends), deu Freund/companion, spa companero/amigo, hin sāthī/mitra (companion/friend), kor chingu/chingudeul (friend/friends). All inflectional forms (singular construct, plural absolute, with pronominal suffixes) share this single sense of personal companionship.
